rules.title: Washington indexes its $1,000,000 deduction every second October from 2029, by one year’s inflation, for that year’s own tax year
rules.conventionRationale: The act uses the same words for the tax year whose return is due the next year: sections 204 and 205 begin in tax year 2028 with taxes due in 2029. The Department applies the identical wording of the capital gains tax (RCW 82.87.150) to the tax year in which each adjustment is made: its page lists the deduction for 2025, set after the 2025 adjustment, as the latest, with none yet for 2026. The plan’s general inflation stands in for the consumer price index the section names. The session law carries line numbers, so each quote stops at a line end and resumes after an elision.
rules.contraryReading: The adjustment made each October applies to the next tax year, so the first change is for 2030: taxes due in the following calendar year read as the following tax year. The deduction would then be $1,000,000 for 2029 and a year behind after, the same in even years and one step lower in odd ones. At 2.5% a year a single filer with $1,500,000 of Washington base income would owe $2,475 more for 2029 ($49,500 against $47,025), $2,574 more for 2031 ($47,025 against $44,451) and $2,673 more for 2035 ($41,877 against $39,204).
